MARKET.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual-occasion wines
MARKET.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: ProWine Shanghai drew over 620 exhibitors from 34 countries and regions plus 21,800 trade visitors this year.
Spain's Rioja, Catalonia, Castilla y León, Toro and Yecla exhibited separately, each highlighting its own growing conditions and styles.
Nearly 90 Chinese wineries exhibited, including producers from Xinjiang, Ningxia and Yantai, stressing regional identity.

MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC dinner menu circulates
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine, made by Guangzhou ShunChangYuan in Conghua, was served at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen.
After the menu circulated online, one Yueli flagship store reported revenue up 93,393.10% and about 5,000 orders within two hours.
The producer began emergency restocking, and several products were listed as sold out, though the comparison period was not specified.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup: Jim Beam pause, record-low wine output, more
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on the continued production pause at Jim Beam’s main facility, dismal estimates for the 2026 global wine...
takeaways: Jim Beam's main facility remains under a continued production pause, according to this week's roundup.
Estimates for global wine production in 2026 are dismal, with output described as remaining at a record low.

MARKET.head: Lynch-Bages issues panda-twin labels to fund Ocean Park conservation
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux classified growth Château Lynch-Bages has released limited-edition wines featuring Hong Kong’s first giant panda twins, pairing a celebration of their birth with fundraising for panda conservation
takeaways: Château Lynch-Bages released limited-edition 2024 wines with labels featuring Hong Kong's giant panda twins Jia Jia and De De, born at Ocean Park.
A charity auction of three-, six- and nine-liter bottles will send all proceeds to Ocean Park's giant panda conservation and education work.
The commemorative wines will be sold in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, distributed in Hong Kong by Altaya Wines Limited.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang as managing director of Domaine de Long Dai and China.
The move places the Shandong winery and national sales team under one leader for the first time.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, at the estate nine years, leaves at year end.

MARKET.head: Moët & Chandon tops Brand Finance's 2026 wine and Champagne brand value ranking
MARKET.summ: Veuve Clicquot recorded the fastest growth, while Australia’s Penfolds suffered the steepest decline, losing 32% of its brand value. China’s Changyu, a longstanding member of the top 10, fell 22%
takeaways: Brand Finance's 2026 Champagne & Wine 10 ranks Moët & Chandon first at US$2.319 billion, up 12% on 2025.
Veuve Clicquot grew fastest, up 39% to US$1.429 billion, while Penfolds fell 32% to US$776 million.
Brand Finance values brands using the Royalty Relief Method, not wine sales, market share or consumer surveys.

MARKET.head: ASVO names Mark O'Callaghan and Lane Williams as new regional directors
MARKET.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) has announced that the appointment of two new directors at its annual general meeting last week “strengthens the board's national presence and builds its depth of skill as the association moves into 2026/27”. “The new board comprises an excellent diversity of experience...
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology ratified four regional directors at its AGM for the 2026/27 year.
Mark O'Callaghan, Victoria-based managing director of Wine Network Consulting, joins as regional director for Victoria.
Lane Williams, head viticulturist at Leeuwin Estate in Western Australia, joins as regional director for WA, QLD and Tasmania.

MARKET.head: Melbourne Polytechnic makes viticulture and winemaking degree cheaper from 2027
MARKET.summ: Melbourne Polytechnic is expanding access to tertiary viticulture and winemaking education through Commonwealth Supported Places in its Bachelor of Agriculture and Technology (Viticulture and Winemaking) from 2027. As Victoria's only provider of undergraduate degrees in viticulture and winemaking, Melbourne Polytechnic “plays a...
takeaways: Melbourne Polytechnic, Victoria's only provider of undergraduate viticulture and winemaking degrees, will offer Commonwealth Supported Places from 2027.
Annual student contribution for the viticulture and winemaking major falls from $23,160 to $4,908 for eligible domestic students.
Victorian Wine Show offers a $5,000 annual scholarship for the Bachelor of Agriculture and Technology, recently awarded to student Daniel Moshopoulos.

MARKET.head: WineGB to exhibit English and Welsh wines at Amsterdam trade fair in January 2027
MARKET.summ: English and Welsh wine has moved from a niche market to one of the most dynamic cool climate categories in Europe. Producers are gaining international attention for sparkling wines, as
takeaways: WineGB, the English and Welsh wine trade association, will exhibit at Wine Professional in Amsterdam in January 2027.
The stand is run with GREAT, the UK government's international comms programme, and targets Dutch buyers, importers and sommeliers.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission names new marketing director for Canada, Mexico, Central America
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission has appointed Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She most recently was chief executive officer of the Center for Produce Safety, and previously international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
Her role is to strengthen trade relationships and increase demand for fresh California table grapes in those markets.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia opens funding call for innovative grape and wine projects
MARKET.summ: Wine Australia is today launching a competitive call for innovative eligible projects to secure funding from the Research & Innovation Fund (RIF) which is part of the Australian Wine Future Fund (AWFF). The organisation said innovative and groundbreaking projects tackling the wine industry’s most critical challenges will be...
takeaways: Wine Australia launched an Expression of Interest for the Research & Innovation Fund, part of the Australian Wine Future Fund.
The Australian Wine Future Fund targets $50 million over five years from Commonwealth, state government, partner and private sources.
Applications close 23 December 2026, with assessments in early 2027 and quarterly rounds after that.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting over 200 exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
Twelve national pavilions will show more than 1,000 wine and drinks brands, co-organised by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice.
Tariffs on some imported wines and spirits are set to fall under free trade agreements with Australia, the UK, New Zealand and the EU.

CULTURE.head: Bergerac winemakers push fresher, lighter reds and sweet wines free of Bordeaux's shadow
CULTURE.summ: The winemakers of Bergerac are tired of living in the shadow of neighboring Bordeaux , as they should be. The relatively small, hilly French wine region is anchored by the same Dordogne River that flows into Bordeaux. Bergerac, which has seven subregions and 13 appellations, begins about a dozen miles east of the Saint-Émilion...
takeaways: Bergerac winemakers now reject being seen as Bordeaux's cousin, and are officially part of France's South West wine region.
Producers are moving away from heavily oaked, full-bodied reds toward fresher wines, with less extraction and large neutral oak barrels.
Some winemakers report US sales rising under 20% Trump-era tariffs as shoppers switch from pricier Bordeaux and Burgundy to Bergerac.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slips as coffee's did, columnist argues
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: Columnist uses Paul Krugman's 1987 essay 'Is Free Trade Passé?' as a model for asking whether wine is passé.
He says wine sales and alcoholic beverage sales have fallen dramatically, with mocktail lists now sometimes longer than wine lists.
He compares wine to coffee, which he says has moved from a default choice to one option among many.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts the Wine 101 podcast episode featuring Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines.
The conversation covers how Story fell into the wine business, with family and community as the focus.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks.

SCIENCE.head: Gloucestershire vineyard releases First Release white after earliest harvest in 50 years
SCIENCE.summ:
Three Choirs unveils First Release white wine after long, hot summer led to earliest harvest start in 50 years

Forget beaujolais nouveau: a Gloucestershire vineyard has uncorked its 2026 vintage, giving the first taste of this year’s long, hot summer - and an answer to France’s autumn tradition of opening young wine...
takeaways: Three Choirs near Newent, Gloucestershire, unveiled its 2026 First Release white, a dry wine of 5,000 bottles.
First grapes were picked on 20 August, a week earlier than the previous record set in 2025.
The harvest ended 9 October, with 200 tonnes collected across the vineyard's 30 hectares.

SCIENCE.head: Winemakers say vintage quality now depends on adaptive vineyard and cellar decisions
SCIENCE.summ: As unpredictable growing conditions blur the line between good and bad vintages, wine professionals are reconsidering how vintage quality is defined, evaluated, and communicated
takeaways: Napa's 2011 vintage was rated 86 by Wine Spectator and 82 by Wine Advocate despite some wines aging well.
Winemakers including Steve Matthiasson and Philippe Pascal say timing and farming choices now shape vintage quality more than weather alone.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy's Clos Pascal uses electrical conductivity mapping to read soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping from 2021 to find underground soil differences.
Owner Philippe Pascal dug over 30 pits guided by maps at 75 centimeters and 1.5 meters depth, finding varying limestone density.
In 2026, tressed Pinot Noir reached 13.6 percent potential alcohol versus 14.5 percent for a conventionally trimmed neighboring parcel.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its agrochemical and MRL search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google stores.
The free app gives rapid access to information in the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the Dog book.
Users with the app are asked to perform an update to keep receiving app updates; the AWRI helpdesk handles questions.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography’s 2026 Gift Guide for Discerning Wine Lovers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Buying a gift for a serious wine lover can be maddening. The more devoted they are, the better the odds
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Vinography has published a 2026 gift guide aimed at discerning wine lovers, according to its title.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which its regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.
A Cabernet Franc claimed top honours at Maryland's Governor's Cup, per the Cab Franc Chronicles roundup.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Blanc de Noirs Champagnes are white wines made from black grapes Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, because their juice is colourless.
Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, is a red-fleshed teinturier grape bred in 19th-century France by Louis and Henri Bouschet.
Teinturier grapes were bred in the 1800s to add colour to pale wines, and Burgundy producer rumours suggest Alicante Bouschet is grown to boost Pinot Noir colour.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Eight impressive wines from leading independent wine merchant Yapp Brothers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Yapp Brothers are based in Wiltshire, in the southwest of the UK, and are an important importer of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Yapp Brothers, a Wiltshire-based importer and independent merchant, showed eight wines at the Bunch tasting, a collaborative event of independent retailers.
Domaine André Vatan Sancerre Les Charmes 2025 is scored 94/100 at £23.25, described as a benchmark despite the warm year.
Patrick Jasmin Côte-Rôtie La Giroflarie 2022 is the top-scored wine at 95/100, priced at £52.75.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: It says 'minerality' has become a catch-all term, and that 'good sapidity' can make a note sound cosmopolitan.
The author notes that Robert Parker Jr's 'pain grillé' phrasing and endless fruit-salad lists have fallen out of favour.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais bulk prices fell in 2026: Mâcon-Villages Blanc down 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc down 13 per cent, despite bulk white volume rising 5 per cent.
Pouilly-Fuissé was valued at about €817 a hectolitre for the 2024 harvest, versus about €3,050 for Puligny-Montrachet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Choosing Thanksgiving Wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: No single wine pairs perfectly with the Thanksgiving meal, but many styles can shine on your table
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Chardonnay and off-dry Riesling are traditional Thanksgiving wine choices, along with Pinot Noir, Gamay-based Beaujolais, and sparkling wines.
Avoid youthful, jammy, heavily extracted wines, which can feel too heavy with a big meal and overwhelm delicate dishes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics' expertise should sit just above their target audience's level, whether supertasters, winemakers, or mainstream buyers.
Atkin says the American critic model favours tasting ability while the British model favours theoretical knowledge and scholarship.
Atkin criticises the roughly 30-second tasting ritual, noting reviewers often assess tens or even hundreds of wines in one sitting.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources such as local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and cellar consignments.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and images, and Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is available and connects them with the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain dropped to sixth by value in China, below New Zealand, with only Chile's per-liter value slightly lower among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with Guangzhou next on November 6, featuring Piqueras' El Abuelo and DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo.
